Name: European Space Agency - ESA
Description: We are the European Space Agency. Our mission is the peaceful exploration and use of space for the benefit of everyone. We watch over Earth, develop and launch inspiring space projects, train astronauts and push the boundaries of science and technology, seeking answers to the big questions about the Universe. We are scientists, engineers and business professionals from all over Europe working together in a diverse and multinational environment. We are dedicated to united space in Europe and united Europe in space.

Name: EXIMURANCE FPV
Description: EXIMURANCE FPV is a startup aiming to develop high endurance Drone technology, while partnering with key manufacturers globally to make available components of aerial vehicles.

Name: Blue Avation Group GmbH
Description: Blue Aviation ist ein Drohnen TEC & Schulung Startup für Einsätze unter Wasser, über Wasser und an Land. Wir bieten digitalisierte Drohnenschulungen, Drohnen-Consulting und die Entwicklung von Konzepten & Implementierungsstrategien, um Next-Level-Drohnentechnologie mit Kunden und Industrie zu verbinden und neue Anwendungen sowie innovative Einsatzkonzepte in der Praxis umzusetzen.

Name: Caelex
Description:
Compliance intelligence for the European space industry. Caelex automates how space operators monitor, manage, and prove regulatory compliance — across national space laws, cybersecurity frameworks, and authorization regimes.

 Our platform combines predictive compliance modelling with autonomous evidence collection and cryptographically verifiable audit trails — so operators know what's coming before it hits. Built in Berlin for the operators shaping Europe's future in orbit.

Name: Mosae Zorg Industries
Description:
Today's AI can't predict novel threats and quantum hardware is too noisy. MosaeQ solves this with a new class of computer built on a unique, lunar-sourced material with its own cislunar real-estate.  We created,for example,mosaeQ.com  Description
MosaeQ is a cutting-edge Drug Discovery Platform that revolutionizes preclinical assessment through quantum technology. By integrating advanced data analytics and innovative methodologies, MosaeQ accelerates drug development, ensuring precision in compound evaluation and maximizing therapeutic potential. Harnessing the power of quantum insights, MosaeQ stands at the forefront of transformative medicinal advancements.  

We have more projects in our pipeline.
Join us and learn more.

Name: DIANA - Dedicated Infrastructure and Architecture for Near Earth Astronautics
Description: The Dedicated Infrastructure and Architecture for Near-Earth Astronautics (DIANA) is a design concept for a self-sustainable lunar village near the de Gerlache crater, on the lunar South Pole, comprising tourists and astronauts alike. The village will be permanently inhabited and will exploit future technologies to achieve independence from Earth resupply missions. This concept focuses on in-situ resource utilization (ISRU), architecture and scientific research.

Name: Arkatrum UG
Description:
Arkatrum UG empowers space ventures with expert guidance, helping them navigate complexity and deliver mission success.

Arkatrum UG is an official reseller of FreeFlyer, an astrodynamics and mission design software of a.i. solutions, Inc. 

Arkatrum UG is focused on the following services: FreeFlyer Software Introduction, Space Mission Analysis, Space Systems Engineering, Project Planning, Strategy Consulting

Name: Zsombor Sapi Engineering
Description: Offering consultancy in aerospace & space related to hardware design and development, analysis and digitalization

Name: Luna Dynamics
Description:
Luna Dynamics specialises in developing modular digital twin technology for spacecraft and space infrastructure beyond Low Earth Orbit (LEO). Our solutions create high-fidelity virtual representations of satellite and mission systems, enabling operators and engineers to simulate behaviour, assess risk, and optimise operations throughout long-duration missions.

By combining telemetry, physics-based models, and scenario simulation, we support sustainable deep-space exploration through improved mission reliability, operational flexibility, and informed decision-making. 
Our approach focuses on scalable, adaptable digital twins that evolve with the mission, supporting complex space environments and future infrastructure development.

Name: COSMOS Space Corporation
Description: COSMOS will act as a service integrator for the whole LEO market through the first European commercial space station. Our solution, based on the heritage of novel AI-based spacecraft operation software (SW) integrated with lessons learned from the +15 years of ISS operations, offers an unprecedented holistic approach to LEO commercialisation through an automated human-rated infrastructure. Beyond the traditional existing competitor’s space station concept, COSMOS will foster the LEO ecosystem and traffic management while providing new opportunities to reduce customers’ operating costs.

Name: Marineris
Description: Marineris builds, tests and launches fully 3D printed model rockets and creates products for generic purposes. In the not-so-distant future, we aim to support the ongoing efforts of space exploration and establish a sustainable presencce on the Moon, Mars and beyond...

Name: CosmoNews
Description: CosmoNews serves as a hub for space enthusiasts, scientists, and industry professionals to stay updated on the latest developments in astronomy, space exploration, and cutting-edge cosmic discoveries. Featuring daily updates, expert insights, and breaking news on topics ranging from rocket launches to deep-space missions to space tech startups, CosmoNews keeps its audience engaged with high-quality, informative content. Followers can explore articles on NASA, ESA and SpaceX missions, emerging space technologies, and groundbreaking astronomical findings. The page also fosters a community for discussion, networking, and collaboration among space lovers and professionals worldwide. Whether you're an industry expert or simply fascinated by the universe, CosmoNews is your go-to source for staying informed about the ever-evolving cosmos.

Name: Muga Space
Description: Muga Space delivers expert consultancy for space operations, ground segment engineering, systems engineering, quality assurance, and mission security — enabling organisations to operate with confidence in the most demanding domain.

Name: Exolaunch
Description:
Exolaunch is a global leader in launch mission management, satellite integration and satellite deployment technologies. With a decade of flight heritage and 650+ satellites launched across 41 missions to date, Exolaunch leverages industry insight to tailor turnkey solutions that meet customer needs and respond to market trends. Exolaunch fulfills launch contracts for industry leaders, the world's most innovative startups, research institutions, government organizations, and international space agencies. The company develops and manufactures its own flight-proven and industry-leading satellite separation systems and payload launch stacks, with the fastest-growing heritage on the market.

Exolaunch, headquartered in Germany, operates globally with offices in the US, France, and Japan. Exolaunch promotes safe, sustainable, and responsible use of space and is committed to making space accessible for all.

Name: ARQUIMEA
Description:
ARQUIMEA was founded with the purpose of developing technologies, products, and services that help address the challenges and needs of our society. Since 2005, we have been contributing our passion for innovation and technology  to highly demanding sectors:

 Aerospace
 Defense
 Science Industry
 Fintech

We firmly believe that technology is the key to progress . That is why we reinvest most of our profits in the development of innovative solutions for the sectors in which we operate.

 We operate in 40 countries, allowing us to stay close to our customers worldwide.

At ARQUIMEA, we all share a strong passion for technology. We are constantly seeking new and exciting challenges that enable us to keep moving forward .

Name: ATMOS Space Cargo
Description:
ATMOS Space Cargo designs and manufactures space capsules to return any cargo – from below 100 kg to multiple tons – from space.
Our technology will offer microgravity on demand, ranging from only 3 hours to 3 months in orbit.
ATMOS will enter the market with a first demonstration mission in 2025.

Name: EUSI
Description: European Space Imaging (EUSI) has led the earth observation sector in Europe for more than 20 years, providing the best Very High Resolution (VHR) satellite imagery commercially available. The first to bring 30 cm resolution satellite imagery to the European market, we are firmly established as the most trusted source for efficient collection and Near Real-Time (NRT) delivery of high-quality satellite imagery products. Through our ground station at the German Aerospace Center, we continue to directly access the most advanced optical imagery satellites in the world and propel Europe into the next age of remote sensing technologies.

Name: Vyoma
Description: Vyoma is a Munich-based company that leverages space-based and ground-based data to empower automated satellite operations and deliver space intelligence to the industry. Officially founded in August 2020, Vyoma offers services that enable efficient and scalable satellite operations in congested orbits around Earth, drastically reducing mission costs for its customers. Vyoma tenders to operators, space commands and space agencies. As a participant in the European Commission and ESA programs for SDA technology development, Vyoma relies on a specialized workforce of 40+ engineers and scientists.

Name: FarEarth Labs
Description:
For Earth observation missions.

Processing and data management software platform for Earth observation satellites.

We support thermal, multispectral, hyperspectral, and more. FarEarth is the easiest way to calibrate imagers and rapidly roll out processing from raw to analysis-ready imagery.

FarEarth provides on-board processing for low-latency applications, as well as high-throughput precision image processing for intelligence applications.

We understand each satellite and camera is unique. We use our expert science to review your camera lab data, calibrate your imager, assist with your satellite's commissioning, and streamline your processing pipeline in the FarEarth platform. 

You can also create your own workflows and scale downstream processing in our platform. FarEarth easily handles multiple constellations.

Our managed subscription service grows with your requirements. We are there to support you with your daily production processing.

Name: AIRMO
Description:
AIRMO is an international climate and space tech company with German roots. We monitor methane emissions using proprietary instruments: spectrometer and atmospheric LiDAR. Our machine learning learning algorithm runs processing enabling leakage detection and quantification. 

We use in-house built instruments to measure methane from the ground, from the air, and - starting next year - from space. 

We are a VCs and European Space Agency (ESA) backed startup with the goal to become the global leader in methane emissions monitoring.

Name: SpaceFounders
Description:
SpaceFounders is a unique European community driving momentum in the space industry. 

A partnership between the French space Agency, the Italian space agency and the Bundeswehr University Munich, we’re uniquely placed to bring private and public sector pioneers together to create the space leaders of tomorrow.

Name: ISPRS - International Society for Photogrammetry and Remote Sensing
Description: The International Society for Photogrammetry and Remote Sensing is a non-governmental organization devoted to the development of international cooperation for the advancement of photogrammetry and remote sensing and their applications. The Society operates without any discrimination on grounds of race, religion, nationality, or political philosophy.

Name: Omnidea
Description:
"Our mission is to contribute to the expansion of human society's frontier. Our society is a global system nowadays, through the universal laws of physics it tends to become homogeneous. Therefore, the only way to ensure a general growth is to keep constantly expanding the boundaries of our activity."

We have a multidisciplinary team of highly qualified professionals with comprehensive engineering backgrounds, who provide solutions to the challenges inherent to the aerospace industry, namely in the development of propulsion systems, airborne platforms and advanced manufacturing technologies.

Omnidea is part of Omnidea Group composed by Omnidea (PT), Omnidea-RTG (DE), Armilar (PT) and Pleione (GR), all dedicated to the aerospace industry.

Name: Spaceopal
Description:
Spaceopal is the Galileo Service Operator, delivering end-to-end service operations for Europe’s global satellite navigation system.
On behalf of EUSPA, Spaceopal ensures continuous, secure, and reliable Galileo positioning, navigation, and timing services for billions of users worldwide. As a strong example of Italian-German cooperation, Spaceopal combines expertise to operate, maintain, and evolve Galileo’s services — supporting Europe’s strategic autonomy, innovation, and technological leadership.

Name: MBS GmbH
Description:
MBS is an owner-managed mid-sized German space company operating globally. We operate full-scale responsive space missions and provide space-based applications as-a-service. 

With over 45 years of experience we run ground segments in Germany and Europe, provide European launch capabilities and own satellites in orbit. Our focus is on ad-hoc capabilities for in-theatre mission support, covering aspects as mission critical communications, situational awareness and managed gateway services on a global scale. Our international government and industry customers trust MBS’s quality, integrity and combat proven expertise.

Name: Max Planck Institute for Solar System Research (MPS)
Description:
The research focus of the Max Planck Institute for Solar System Research is our cosmic neighborhood: the solar system with its planets and moons, comets and asteroids as well as the sun. The aim of the scientists is to describe the processes in the solar system in models and to simulate them on the computer. In addition, instruments are being developed and built to study these bodies from space. The Institute is involved in numerous space missions.

The institute is organized in three scientific departments and further research groups.

- Department Sun and Heliosphere
- Planetary Science Department
- Department Solar and Stellar Interiors

Name: CinSOIL
Description:

Name: 5th Symposium on Space Educational Activities
Description: The Symposium on Space Educational Activities (SSEA), organised by the European Space Agency’s Education Office, provides a forum for university students, professionals working in education, and other young professionals to present and discuss their experiences organising, running and/or participating in Educational Activities related to Space.

Name: Vanguard Technology
Description: High power rockets, rocket motors, stratospheric balloons and circuits

Name: Ethereal Space
Description:
Ethereal Space is the first commercial company to build a dedicated space weather satellite constellation as a sentry to monitor potentially hazardous solar activity and conditions on the Sun, in the solar wind, magnetosphere and ionosphere which can degrade, damage, or devastate all spacecraft in orbit and the Earth-based industries which rely upon them.

Our team is comprised of aerospace and defense industry professionals who have spent their careers in space. From the design and development of science missions for both GEO and LEO, to the spacecraft and instruments such as: multispectral and hyperspectral spectrometers, passive microwave and infrared atmospheric sounders, ozone profilers, GNSS Radio Occultation, GNSS Reflectometry, Electro-Optical/Infrared Imagers, and radar altimeters. The Ethereal Space team has successfully designed and led multiple space missions including satellite assembly, integration, test, launch and operations. Our work included the US Government, Foreign Governments, and Civil/Commercial missions globally.

Name: LYRASENSE
Description:
LYRASENSE is the agentic AI platform for satellite intelligence. It is purpose-built for teams that need to turn satellite data into operational decisions, fast.
The world generates more data from space than ever before. Yet for most organizations - defense operators, disaster response teams, infrastructure managers - accessing, processing and deploying that data remains slow, fragmented and technically prohibitive.
LYRASENSE changes that. Our Geo Agentic SwarmTM handles the full stack: from ingesting satellite data to deploying production-ready applications, on Earth or on orbit, all through a single, intelligent platform. No complex GIS workflows. No endless handoffs and procurement cycles. No bottlenecks.
From wildfire detection and flood mapping to oil spill monitoring and mission-critical intelligence, LYRASENSE empowers operators and decision-makers to deploy their own solutions in minutes. 

Satellite intelligence, operationalized.

Name: SeRANIS - Mission
Description: SeRANIS "Seamless Radio Access Networks for Internet of Space" is the world's first and only small satellite mission to provide a publicly accessible multifunctional experimental laboratory in orbit.

Name: iSEE - Impact Space Expedition and Exploration
Description: iSEE (Impact Space Expedition & Exploration) is a global leader in space security, providing advanced multi sensing AI controlled technology for Space Situational and Domain Awareness (SSDA)

Name: IMS Space Consultancy GmbH
Description: We are a dynamic company operating in the field of the satellite engineering and operations, currently providing consultancy for European Space Agencies. Our experience spans from Spacecraft Design to Operations and has grown in the years through the development of challenging projects and collaborations with a wide range of industrial partners and international organizations. The services provided by IMS include specialized consulting, project support, software development, and research.

Name: Parametry.ai
Description:
Parametry.ai is an innovation lab developing AI, decentralized systems, and trusted digital infrastructure for complex, high-stakes environments.

Our work focuses on one fundamental challenge: enabling large-scale collaboration between organizations, autonomous systems, and intelligent agents without relying on a single point of trust.

From space traffic management and orbital safety to sovereign cloud infrastructure, AI governance, and supply-chain transparency, we design technologies that make collaboration more transparent, explainable, and resilient.

Our projects include Space DAO, decentralized consensus systems for space operations, AI-powered decision support and risk assessment, open-source agent technologies, and European cloud infrastructure built for performance, sovereignty, and sustainability.

We partner with research institutions, industry leaders, and public organizations to transform ambitious ideas into operational systems.

Engineering trust for the next generation of autonomous collaboration.

Name: Panopterra
Description:
Panopterra specializes in advanced Artificial Intelligence and Deep Learning for Earth Observation and geospatial applications. We combine expertise in computer vision, evolutionary learning, and large-scale data processing with deep domain knowledge. By integrating scientific rigor with technical innovation, we transform complex datasets into actionable insights that power monitoring, prediction, and analysis – enabling data-driven Earth Intelligence.

Founded in 2020, Panopterra collaborates with partners and clients worldwide on research, development, and operational projects. We are dedicated to delivering scientifically grounded, innovative, and dependable solutions that create tangible, lasting value. Through close collaboration and a strong scientific foundation, we support clients in harnessing advanced technologies effectively, enabling informed decisions and addressing complex real-world challenges across sectors.

Name: Responsive Space Cluster Competence Center (RSC3)
Description: The Responsive Space Cluster Competence Center (RSC3) is the center of expertise within the German Aerospace Center (DLR) for all topics related to Responsive Space, i.e., the timely deployment and provision of space-borne capabilities. The RSC3 was founded in September 2020 and is funded by the German Federal Ministry of Defence. It is tasked with establishing a technology base for Responsive Space and conducting technology demonstrations in this field. To this end, the RSC3 follows a holistic approach. With the entire space and security ecosystem in view, RSC3 aims to identify more responsive ways to provide actionable data and information from orbit. This is reflected by the organization of the RSC3 into four departments: Launch Segment, Ground Segment, Space Segment and Technology Demonstration. The RSC3 is focused on connecting existing expertise within industry and the research community and to develop in close exchange with the user (the Bundeswehr, German Federal Armed Force and the Federal Ministry of Defence) a roadmap for a responsive and resilient space infrastructure. In this context, RSC3 provides to the user independent analysis and evaluation of Responsive Space concepts. The RSC3 is growing and always looking for skilled and motivated future colleagues. If you take an interest in “thinking outside the box” to develop the space into a responsive infrastructure, do not hesitate to contact us. You can reach us at: info-rs@dlr.de Impressum: https://www.dlr.de/DE/Service/Impressum/impressum_node.html Privacy Policy: https://www.dlr.de/EN/Service/PrivacyPolicy/privacypolicy2.html

Name: STAR Dresden e.V.
Description: We are a university group at TU Dresden and want to test our excellent scientific education in exciting and challenging hands-on space projects. For this purpose, we participate in various programs and challenges, such as the ERC Space and Robotics Event or the German-Swedish REXUS/BEXUS program. We develop various hardware and software for these projects ourselves to test and develop our skills as engineers and scientists and to improve our teamwork.

Name: Myriad - Autonomous Gardening
Description: We believe everyone should have the opportunity to grow their own vegetables – no matter if they live in an urban metropolis, the desert or in space. To achieve this, we use the most innovative technologies to develop efficient and user-friendly products. We build Autonomous Gardens that fit into every home and lifestyle.

Name: Future Space Architecture
Description: Future Space Architecture (FSA) is an innovative startup dedicated to reshaping the future of space logistics through the development of cutting-edge in-orbit infrastructures. Founded by space architect Omar Alayli, FSA operates at the intersection of aerospace, technology, and space engineering design to provide reliable, cost-effective, and efficient solutions that drive the space industry’s growth.

Name: Polimak Space
Description:
Advancing the frontier of space exploration through ground-breaking ISRU and bulk solids handling solutions, Polimak is redefining the realm of possibilities.

In-situ resource utilization (ISRU) — the use of local resources found on extraterrestrial bodies like the Moon or Mars — is a key pivot in space exploration. It offers the promise of sustained human life and operations, reducing the need for costly, challenging transportation of materials from Earth. From extracting water to manufacturing rocket propellants, ISRU stands at the brink of ushering in a new era of extraterrestrial civilization.

Leveraging our extensive know-how in designing and producing top-tier space mining technologies, we bring the concept of ISRU to life. Our comprehensive range of solutions encompasses processing, conveying, storage, dust mitigation, and feeding systems, essential for efficient resource extraction from celestial bodies such as the Moon, Mars, and asteroids.

As an engineering firm with a deep-rooted specialty in bulk solids handling technologies, Polimak brings 40 years of industry expertise to the forefront of space exploration. We've evolved from providing solutions for industrial processes to offering advanced solutions for the excavation, processing, and handling of lunar, asteroid, and Martian regolith.

Our ISRU solutions are ingeniously designed to minimize dependence on Earth-based resources, thereby reducing the environmental footprint of space mining operations. With our extensive experience in bulk solids handling, we customize systems to meet specific requirements, optimizing resource recovery in the process.

Polimak's mission echoes the spirit of pioneering: to enable efficient and sustainable space exploration. Together, we're venturing into the uncharted, making the infinite accessible.

Name: Institut für Navigation
Description: The Institute of Navigation (INS) at the University of Stuttgart is involved in the development and testing of navigation solutions and the corresponding mathematical foundations.

Name: Space Debris DAO
Description:
Space belongs to everyone, and at Space Debris DAO, we're committed to ensuring that it remains accessible for future generations.

To preserve space and keep it accessible for future missions, we are developing a decentral organization (DAO) that incentivizes sustainable practices. Our goal is to keep space accessible, usable, and sustained for everyone.

Our Mission
The Space Debris DAO is a decentralized autonomous organization (DAO) dedicated to promoting sustainable space standards and addressing the growing issue of orbital debris. We envision a future where space is a clean and safe environment for all, and we believe that blockchain technology can play a key role in bringing stakeholder together globally.

Our Approach
The Space Debris DAO connects stakeholders from across the space industry, including satellite operators, launch providers, researchers, and policymakers. We leverage blockchain technology to create a transparent and decentralized governance structure that empowers our members to collaborate on innovative solutions to space debris mitigation.

Join our virtual community events

Name: SpaceOps
Description:
The International Committee on Technical Interchange for Space Mission Operations and Ground Data Systems (also referred to as the SpaceOps Organization) was formed in the realization that given the large number of people involved in space mission operations, an organized community or technical forum is needed. Since mission operations have become an increasingly large segment of space agency budgets, there is great interest in improving the capabilities and cost efficiencies of mission operations. It was in the spirit of providing the broadest possible managerial and technical interchange between space agencies, academia, and industry that SpaceOps was established.


Since its inception in 1990, SpaceOps has held fifteen biennial conferences hosted by various countries around the world. This international forum discusses state-of-the-art operations principles, methods, and tools and provide an opportunity to foster managerial and technical interchange on all aspects of space mission operations, including such areas as robotics, human, earth orbiting, and deep space aspects of space operations.

Name: ASTRAEUS e.V.
Description: The ASTRAEUS research association supports science, research, technical applications and international cooperation in the field of space technology, especially human space flight and exploration.

Name: Space DAO
Description:
Space DAO is a a professional community driven initiative to enhance the reliabilty of space data for SSA and STM. Our mission is to foster collaboration and consensus on space data to ensure its quality. Therefore, we use Blockchain technology as consensus mechanism to reduce risks associated with a single dominant entity controlling vital information for decision-making.

Key Features:

1. Consensus Mechanism and Governance: Space DAO effectively establishs consensus on measurements and data from multiple sources.

2. Data Trust Augmentation: By combining data from various sources, Space DAO enhances quality assurance through network consensus.

3. Network Consensus Distribution: Users can evaluate data conformity using the platform's consensus distribution.

4. Delta to Network Consensus: Providers can benchmark their data against network consensus, ensuring their data quality assurance and improvement.

5. Space Data Marketplace: Space DAO provides a thriving marketplace for high quality space data insights and analytics



Space DAO empowers a diverse range of stakeholders to contribute and benefit:


- Satellite operators can use Space DAO to enhance their Space Situational Awareness (SSA)

- Data providers who sell and share information, measurements and analyses

- Space Data users who leverage Space DAO knowledge for their projects

- Regulators and Space Policy makers who develop rules for space traffic, disaster response, or other space applications


Space DAO is open for collaboration with stakeholder in space. Reach out to us for any request on information, partnership or contributions.

Name: Darius Pro
Description: Darius Pro is a space project management and satellite communication consulting firm. We offer Project Management and Engineering consultancy for governments, educational institutions and corporations. Our major fields of expertise is design and development of TT&C and Remote Sensing ground stations, link budgets, wave propagation modeling, EM and Mechanical simulations.

Name: euconvest GmbH
Description:
euconvest GmbH is based in Bavaria’s Aerospace Hub Ottobrunn.

Our goal is to bridge the gap between commercial space research, space innovation, market positioning, and private investment.

We work with space startups, scale-ups, and innovation-driven organisations as strategic advisors and sparring partners, supporting them in strengthening their business logic, investor readiness, and communication at critical growth and funding moments.

With over 30 years of experience in private banking and finance and more than 10 years of experience in space communications and space policy, euconvest GmbH combines financial expertise, sector insight, and strategic communication to support sustainable growth in the European space economy.

Name: Exlumina, Inc.
Description:
Exlumina is building orbital data centers to process data directly in space.

The company develops GPU-powered orbital compute infrastructure that enables real-time data processing, artificial intelligence inference, and autonomous decision-making directly in orbit.

Modern satellites generate massive volumes of information, but transmitting raw data to Earth introduces latency, bandwidth limitations, and high downlink costs. Exlumina addresses this challenge by deploying compute-enabled satellites capable of processing and optimizing data before it is transmitted to ground stations.

By transforming satellites from passive sensors into active compute nodes, Exlumina enables new capabilities for satellite operators, AI companies, research institutions, and defense systems.

Operating internationally with engineering and research activities in Europe and the Middle East, Exlumina is building the computational foundation for the emerging space-native economy.

Name: SQAT project
Description:
SQAT is a 3.5-year project, funded under the Horizon Europe Programme, that focuses on Implementing Smart Farming Applications using EO Data, Soil Sensors & Robotics.

SQAT's smart soil mapping service is a multi-level, multi-technology and multi-purpose solution. With a keen eye on markets and users, SQAT’s approach is designed to overcome today’s practical, technical and financial challenges to generate high resolution soil properties maps and demand-driven products like application maps for soil improvement or crop management, or compliancy proof for eco schemes. Our vision is that the integration of different technologies provides a flexible and agile service beating the unbundled alternatives that are now in the market: our in-situ sampling and/or sensoring is wrapped in a Copernicus-based artificial intelligence soil mapping product.

Name: FLuorescence EXplorer (FLEX) project office | Projektbüro
Description:
is a satellite that will provide new insights into the photosynthesis of vegetation from 2025 onwards. The German FLEX project office is an interface between the European Space Agency (ESA) and the German users of FLEX data. Our goal is to prepare the German user community for FLEX. Name: outerspace. agency - OSA
Description: The outerspace. agency (OSA) is Europe's gateway to space communication. Its mission is to shape the narrative of Europe's Space, New Space, and Deep Space Tech sectors, ensuring that innovations in space are clearly communicated and continue to reach audiences across Europe and the world.

Name: Quantum Galactics GmbH
Description:
Quantum Galactics GmbH
Make Space a Safer Place.

Quantum Galactics is a Berlin-based New Space company developing highly integrated electronics and complete 1U CubeSat platforms for rapid, secure, and cost-effective access to space.

 What we deliver
1) QG-1U “1 Unit for Everything” – a fully integrated CubeSat bus for technology demonstration, training, and dual-use applications.
2) CyBER OBC – a Linux-capable, cybersecure, and energy-efficient on-board computer with ECSS/PUS compliance and versatile interfaces.
3) Galactic EPS – modular, passivatable power systems for high availability and seamless integration.

 Why Quantum Galactics?
- Fast & cost-effective – short lead times through in-house manufacturing and national partners.
- Secure & resilient – end-to-end cybersecurity design, CCSDS/ECSS-compliant.
- Flight-proven – systems in orbit since 2025, with documented qualification and operations heritage.

Made in Germany – development, integration, and testing in Berlin.

We work with research, government, and industry customers, supporting various kinds of missions in Germany, the EU and beyond.

Turnkey 1U solutions. Rapid. Resilient. Reliable.

Name: Rover to Mars
Description: Developing and designing a rover, capable of performing crash-site forensics: Find and reach the location(s) of a crashed lander, record the GPS coordinates locations of the lander, equipment servicing, surface sampling, search and rescue, traversal and transport.

Name: NanoFF-Nanosatellites in Formation Flight
Description:
The NanoFF mission, conducted at the Chair of Space Technology at TU Berlin, aims to demonstrate both manual and autonomous close-proximity formation flight capabilities using two CubeSats in Low Earth Orbit. Deployed from an orbital transfer vehicle into a carefully designed helix orbit in January 2024, the CubeSat formation ensures passive collision safety and stability. The mission's objectives include the technology demonstration of deployable solar panels, star-trackers, S-band downlink, and a resistojet propulsion system. The primary payload is an Earth Observation camera system with four spectral channels.

Additionally, the satellites are equipped with an ultra-high frequency based inter-satellite link for data exchange during autonomous formation flight operations and precise navigation supported by multi-constellation GNSS receivers and laser retro-reflectors. The NanoFF mission showcases cutting-edge space technology and paves the way for future advancements in satellite formation flight, close proximity operations and Earth observation.

Name: Hamburg Space Team e.V.
Description: Hamburg Space Team (HST) is a student-led space engineering initiative designing and flying satellites, rockets, and sounding rocket experiments - turning student ideas into real, flight-ready hardware.

Name: ASTRA Bonn - Astropolitics, Strategy & Technology Research Association
Description:
ASTRA Bonn – Astropolitics, Strategy & Technology Research Association
is a student-led research association focused on the political, strategic and technological dimensions of space.

It is conceived as an interdisciplinary platform for students who want to better understand how space activities shape international politics, security and technological development. Our discussions address topics such as space policy, international security, technology and industrial policy, as well as questions of governance. To engage with these issues, we bring together approaches from the social sciences, engineering, economics and natural sciences, alongside law and philosophy.

Our aim is to foster meaningful interdisciplinary exchange, support emerging scholars, and provide an academic platform for informed discussion on how space is reshaping global order.

Name: MUnique Technology GmbH
Description:
Our vision is to have answers to the questions of tomorrow. This includes to be on top of current technological development especially in optical physics. Strong investment in research and out-of-the-box-thinking are key factors in the constant evolution of MUnique Technology to find the best solution for customers ́needs.

Our DORT (Dynamic Optical Ranging & Timing) system is an optical pulsed device which offers a new high precise distance measurement. It has performances some orders of magnitudes better compared to other state of the art technologies like LIDAR. This system is originally developed for space application but can be used on ground as well. 
Thanks to the compact and robust design, DORT can be implemented in very small satellites, so called CubeSats (New Space).

In the terrestrial domain, DORT is also used for a wide range of applications, e.g. structural health monitoring of infrastructure structures, large volume metrology, vibration & shock measurements, and strain measurements.

In addition, we ensure safe satellite operation by providing real-time data on requested orbits and timely notification for potential collisions.

AcTLabS is a young company based in Munich, Germany. In the heart of the European manufacturing market, our team combines years of experience and expertise in space surveillance, machine learning, and software engineering to push space sustainability to new horizons.

Name: Spaceship EAC - Over the Dusty Moon
Description:
Student team from the Spaceship EAC initiative at the European Astronaut Center from the European Space Agency in Cologne, participating in the Over the Dusty Moon challenge of the Colorado School of Mines and Lockheed Martin. 

The challenge consist on the design and construction of a transport system for regolith that is suitable for the lunar conditions. Our system was selected for the final phase, which it will be tested and assessed in Colorado this June during a field campaign. Name: EXPATS-IDEAS4S
Description:
EXPATS is a junior research group funded by the German Weather Service (DWD) within the IDEA-S4S network. 
IDEA-S4S is a new bilateral collaboration between Germany and italy in meteorology, climatology, and related disciplines that will create a center of excellence for cutting-edge research and translate the results into improving operational services and university training. 

EXPATS lives in the time frame 2023-2027. It will develop new cutting-edge research on extreme precipitating events over the Alps, exploiting the high-resolution data provided by the new Meteosat third-generation satellite (MTG) data, and it will collaborate with DWD and ARPAE to bring research results as soon as possible to the operational weather services, and thus beneficial for the society.

Name: HSM Aries.space
Description:
HSM Aries.space is a student-led space systems research initiative based at Hochschule Schmalkalden.
We design and develop autonomous planetary rovers, experimental rocketry systems, and advanced control architectures for space applications. Our interdisciplinary team brings together engineering students from robotics, mechatronics, and embedded systems—guided by academic mentors and industry professionals.

Our flagship project, LEAP-One, focuses on terrain navigation, modular payload design, and onboard autonomy—targeted for participation in international competitions like the European Rover Challenge.

Aries.space offers hands-on experience in simulation, sensor fusion, motion planning, power systems, and systems engineering. We aim to bridge academic research and practical aerospace development, creating a launchpad for future space technologists.

We welcome collaboration with research institutes, corporate sponsors, and hardware partners who share our vision of advancing student-driven innovation in space exploration.

Name: Akilaris
Description:
Akilaris is a Space Intelligence Platform that provides autonomous AI-powered space traffic management.

The company is addressing the critical challenge of space safety, with over 5 million objects orbiting Earth at 17,500 mph, posing collision risks that could trigger cascading failures (Kessler Syndrome).
Key Points:
•	Mission: Transform reactive space surveillance into proactive, autonomous traffic management
•	Solution: AI agents that predict and prevent collisions before they occur, operating like "air traffic control for space" but with superhuman capabilities
•	Technology: Real-time tracking, predictive analytics, and automated collision avoidance with sub-second threat assessment
•	Partnership: Selected ESA BIC Northern Germany 
•	Market: Targeting the €50B+ space economy, serving satellite operators from startups to mega-constellations
•	Impact: Aims to achieve zero collisions for managed assets, 50% reduction in fuel costs for avoidance maneuvers, and 99.999% uptime for critical space services
•	Location: Bremen

The platform democratizes access to space safety infrastructure, enabling the sustainable growth of the space economy while preventing catastrophic orbital debris cascades.

Name: ParaLoon
Description:
We develop deployable "parabolic balloon" concentrator photovoltaic (CPV) systems to provide solar power & process heat for applications in space and on earth. 

Applications in space would include satellites, space stations, planetary habitats or (deep space) mission vehicles. On earth, these structures could be used for off-grid power & heat in remote areas, recreational / defense / refugee or other campsites, emergency situations or mobile applications.

The ParaLoon system combines lightweight, deployable, parabolic reflector structures and different energy conversion technologies, e.g. concentrator photovoltaic (CPV) technologies, for the efficient conversion of solar energy to electric energy and optionally also (industrial) process heat or hot water. 

If wireless power beaming becomes a reality, the electric energy could also be transferred to users in space, on Earth or even on the Moon or Mars by satellites or a satellite network in the future.

With access to massive volumes of complex climatic and risk data derived from multiple sources, you can easily integrate the insights you need and enhance the automated calculations and workflows of your business! Name: TUM Chair of Space Mobility and Propulsion
Description:
Our research interests include: propulsion systems and operations concepts for sustainable and autonomous spacecraft ; democratisation of access to space through innovative space transportation system; health monitoring and innovative AI and data-based control systems for versatile space mobility. 
Space is a critical infrastructure on which we rely for weather information and forecasting, for climate action, for bank transactions, for secured communication and much more. The growing use of space demands long-term reliable, affordable, and scalable solutions for in-space mobility and propulsion. Further the topics contribute to the advancement of terrestrial technologies and markets 
We aim to advance knowledge and bring innovation to space mobility and propulsion and to create an intertwined research and teaching environment.

The event embraces collaborative problem solving with the goal of producing open-source solutions to challenges we currently face on Earth and in space.

During the Space Apps Challenge in 2021, we saw more than 28,000 community members join as participants while 323 Local Leads, and 50 Ambassadors joined to support those participants. Space Apps is a NASA-led initiative organized in collaboration with Booz Allen Hamilton, Mindgrub and SecondMuse.

This year it will take place virtually and in person over 2 days for cities around the globe between October 1st and 2nd, 2022. Details on this year’s event can be found at http://spaceappschallenge.org

Name: MVIPER - Magnetohydrodynamic Vortex-Inducing Photobioreactor Experiment

The experiment is intended for the ESA Academy Experiments Programme 2024/25 and operates under the support and supervision of the Professorship of Human Spaceflight Technology of the Technical University of Munich.

We are an AI-driven Earth observation company building the intelligence layer between satellites and the people who feed the world. Our platform fuses radar, multispectral and hyperspectral data into actionable outputs for two industries:

Agricultural Insurance. Automated SAR-based storm damage detection that reduces field visits by up to 90% and delivers damage assessments in 48 hours instead of 2–4 weeks. Trusted by leading European crop insurers.

Precision Farming. AI-generated Variable Rate Irrigation maps and crop health analytics that have demonstrated 20% water and energy savings on 1,000+ hectares of large-scale operations in the MENA region.

Founded in 2026 by two former Airbus Defence & Space engineers and an AI lead with deep agricultural domain expertise. Headquartered in Munich; operations across Europe, Egypt and the broader MENA region.

Name: SOLER Project
Description:
The SOLER Project has received funding from the European Union's Horizon Europe research and innovation programme (Grant agreement ID: 101134999). 

This project will investigate the most energetic phenomena occurring at the Sun and provide new knowledge on their interrelations, variability and energy partitioning. 

Using the newly expanded unprecedented heliospheric spacecraft fleet we investigate energetic solar eruptions starting from three perspectives: fast coronal mass ejections (CMEs), strong X-ray flares, and large solar energetic particle (SEP) events. Key parameters of the various eruption phenomena will be determined and their interrelations examined to make significant leaps in our understanding on how the eruptive phenomena are linked to each other, how they interact with each other, and how they result in acceleration and release of high energy particles from the solar corona into interplanetary (IP) space. 

Because of their direct link to particle energisation, large-amplitude coronal waves and shocks related to these events will be in focus as well. Magnetic connections of sources with each other and with the in-situ observers will be determined. 

In addition to producing significant amounts of new scientific knowledge in the field, SOLER will provide the wider scientific community a wide array of advanced data products, and novel data analysis and visualisation tools that will be openly distributed. This will greatly facilitate future interdisciplinary studies of energetic solar eruptions.

Name: SpiCy BEXUS
Description:
Team SpiCy was born as a group of students from very different backgrounds with a common purpose: long-term oxygen production for space exploration. 

The team is based in Munich and the members are pursuing Bachelor’s and Master’s degrees in Biology, Aerospace and Electrical Engineering and Communication and Media in the LMU, TUM and HM.

For fulfilling that purpose, our multidisciplinary team has the mission to study the viability of Cyanobacteria in biological Life Support Systems.

To assess the viability of our biological solution, we have to test our hypothesis and we chose the Programme REXUS/BEXUS for it. We have been selected for the BEXUS 15th Cycle. The project is supported by DLR, SNSA and ESA Education Office.

The launch of our experiment to the stratosphere will take place in Kiruna during October 2024. To reach that point, the team has been invited to workshops and training weeks in the main European hubs for space reasearch like DLR HQ in Bonn, ESRANGE in Kiruna and ESTEC in the Netherlands. In all these initiatives, the team has to prove that their experiment and design where properly defined for the mission ahead. 

Throughout the process, we had the chance to meet students and professionals with our same interests in space research!

Name: WarpDrive RWA
Description:
A constantly growing consumption of energy resources requires  more  active reinvention of existing data related to the electromagnetic field as the most fundamental, convenient and widely applied principle in all fields of electrical engineering. The analysis of existing theoretical and practical data of the field theory description mainly the electromagnetic field was carried out. Artificial calibrations and mistakes were found. The condition where the canceled second part of the electromagnetic field allocates fully was stated. Experiments demonstrated that this component does not interact with iron filings, but interacts between one another specifically with a conductor by which an electric current and gravity flow. The main purpose is to test theoretical data in practice. To achieve the stated above purpose, a laboratory machine was engineered and assembled, thereby allowing testing physically all theoretically grounded and modeled data.

Open verification tool — Ew2R3.org: the orbital parameter E = ω2R3 = GM = μ and surface gravity g = E/R2, computed from an orbital period and a radius alone, without mass and without G. Mean deviation 0.06% across the eight planets; every value is recomputed in the browser. Preprints with DOI are linked. https://ew2r3.org

In recent years, the field has expanded to include terrestrial radio and customized solutions for fiber optic communications. In-house mechanical and electronic development can be completely mapped. Name: SHROOM BEXUS
Description:
Shroom BEXUS is a student-led stratospheric flight experiment developed within the REXUS/BEXUS Programme (17th cycle), organized by DLR and SNSA in cooperation with ESA. The project investigates the radiation-attenuation potential and post-irradiation biological response of selected radiotrophic fungi under near-space conditions.

The experiment exposes multiple fungal samples and ground-reference controls to the stratospheric radiation environment during a high-altitude balloon flight. Individual radiation sensors positioned beneath each sample measure transmitted radiation, enabling quantitative comparison between fungal shielding performance and control media. Environmental parameters including temperature, pressure, and humidity are actively regulated within an airtight payload to ensure controlled and repeatable experimental conditions.

The payload architecture consists of an aluminum structural frame housing isolated sample compartments, integrated radiation sensors, an onboard computer, and a thermal control system. The design prioritizes modularity, sensor fidelity, and compliance with REXUS/BEXUS flight and safety requirements.

Post-flight laboratory analysis focuses on growth kinetics, colony morphology, and final biomass to assess the long-term biological effects of irradiation and to correlate biological response with in-flight radiation exposure. The results aim to evaluate the feasibility of radiotrophic fungi as self-growing, biologically based radiation shielding concepts for future space exploration and habitation scenarios.

The balloon launch campaign is planned for October 2026.

Name: Team MAVERICK
Description:
Planet formation is a mesmerizing, yet challenging, bottom-up process – from cosmic dust to planetary giants. However, this journey is hampered by critical growth barriers that simple collisions alone cannot overcome.

 Our Maverick Approach: We, team MAVERICK from the University of Duisburg-Essen, pose a vital question: What influence do magnetic fields have at this crucial stage? Despite magnetic fields being ubiquitous in the cradles of early planets, their role in forming dust aggregates has been largely overlooked.

This innovative, maverick approach demands to be tested!

 The Mission: Investigate the long-term stability of magnetically connected particle clusters under microgravity conditions.

 The Expected Outcome: We aim to determine the maximum possible size of these aggregates and define critical parameters governing their growth and destruction.

 How We Test It: Our experiment is a candidate for the upcoming REXUS 37/38 Campaign. We plan to utilize the suborbital flight environment to bring this innovative research to reality.

 Join Our Mission! We are actively seeking collaboration, sponsors and scientific exchange to propel MAVERICK toward success.

 Get in touch with us to learn more about our experiment and accompany us on our journey to overcome the barriers in planet formation!

Name: Accessibility for Outer Space

We want to collaborate on reduce the gap between established accessibility best practices and the unique demands of space exploration.

Our mission is to advocate for, research, and drive the integration of inclusive design principles into:

 Spacecraft & Habitats: Ensuring interfaces, controls, and environments are usable by diverse astronauts and crew members, including those with disabilities.

 Ground Support Systems: Applying robust digital accessibility standards to the software, applications, and data systems crucial for mission control and research.

Let's Connect and Collaborate!

Name: Analogue Icy Moon Simulations (AIMS) Project
Description: The Analogue Icy Moon Simulations (AIMS) project, funded by the European Research Council, investigates the physicochemical conditions in the subsurface of icy ocean worlds like Saturn’s moon Enceladus. This small moon is home to diverse chemistry across various regions, and is considered amongst the most likely locations where extraterrestrial life could reside in the solar system. AIMS studies chemistry that can occur in high-pressure and high-temperature regions in the depths of Enceladus’ ocean, how chemical species are modified as they travel from ocean floor to surface, and what spacecraft sampling of Enceladus’ cryovolcanoes can reveal about habitability. Dr. Nozair Khawaja was awarded a Consolidator Grant by the European Research Council for the five-year AIMS research project at Freie Universität Berlin.

Name: Lumo Space
Description:
LUMO Space is building the open standard for cargo logistics and infrastructure on the lunar surface.

Reaching the Moon is becoming routine. Building on it is not, because every payload, subsystem and habitat still solves packaging, integration and transport on its own. There is no shared physical standard for how cargo moves between landers, rovers and habitats.

We change that with HEX, an open, hexagonal standard container for space. Think of it as an ISO container for the Moon, a common housing and interface that any institute or company can build their payload into once and fly on many different missions.

Around that standard we provide the full logistics chain. We house your payload in a HEX container, validate it on Earth through analog campaigns and mock up tests, integrate it, and deliver it across the lunar surface to where it needs to go. One standard, one partner, one contract.

The standard is open by design, so the whole world can build on the Moon together.

AD LUNAM.
